title: Run-Length Encoding
prompt:
In this project directory, implement a Python module named run_length_encoding.py with two functions:
  - encode(s: str) -> str : run-length encodes a string. Each run of 2+ identical consecutive characters becomes '<count><char>' (e.g. 'aaabccc' -> '3abc3c'); a single occurrence stays as just the character with no count.
  - decode(s: str) -> str : reverses encode, expanding '<count><char>' pairs back to repeated characters and leaving lone characters unchanged.
Input strings contain only letters (no digits), which avoids ambiguity between a literal digit and a run count. decode(encode(x)) == x must hold for any such input. There is already a hidden reference test suite at tests/test_run_length_encoding.py -- do NOT modify it. Your Testing phase should run `pytest tests -q` (in addition to any tests you write yourself) and every test must pass. Also add a short README.md explaining the encoding scheme.
